findings.passage: Critics in the Legislature, including Haskins, questioned whether the change would create unnecessary complications for residents and whether existing safeguards already verify voter eligibility.
findings.note: Post on his campaign site, bylined to him, written in the third person (posted Feb 13; year not shown on page). It describes his questions in House debate on a bill to print citizenship status on driver's licenses. Not a first-person quote.

findings.passage: During the debate, Representative Kirk Haskins of Topeka questioned whether additional constitutional language was needed given that Kansas law already requires voters to be U.S. citizens.
findings.note: Campaign-site post (shown Feb 5; the news story it cites is dated 2025-02-04), third person. Says he questioned a proposed constitutional amendment on citizen voting because state law already requires citizenship.

findings.passage: As Kansas voters prepare to decide a constitutional amendment concerning citizenship and voting eligibility, Representative Kirk Haskins is questioning the motivation behind the proposal.
findings.note: Campaign-site post about the 2026 ballot amendment on citizen voting, third person, citing a 2026-10-30 news story. States that he questions the reason for the amendment.

findings.passage: While Haskins described that as a “minor misstep,” he said the larger issue deserves scrutiny, warning that selective attention and bias “damages public trust in our elected officials and ultimately our democracy.”
findings.note: Campaign-site post (date from the news story it cites). He spoke about uneven enforcement of election law after a call to investigate gift cards offered to students registering to vote. Related to voter registration rules, not ID.

findings.passage: As the Kansas Legislature advanced a package of election-related bills altering voting procedures, Representative Kirk Haskins of Topeka participated in ongoing debates over how the changes could affect voters across the state.
findings.note: Campaign-site post, third person, giving no position of his own. Shows he took part in debate on the 2026 election bill package.
